source_refs.note: Book p. 192: 10.5 Half Angle Identities, lead-in sentence and (i) cos a/2, (ii) sin a/2, (iii) tan a/2 with +/- roots; 10.6 begins below on the same page

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne angle ka dugna (\(2\alpha\)) dekha. Aaj ulta safar hai: angle ka aadha, yani \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\). Sawal yeh hai ke agar humein poore angle ka cosine maloom ho, to aadhe angle ka sin, cos aur tan kaise nikalein? Misal ke taur par \(\cos 30^{\circ}\) humein yaad hai; kya us se \(15^{\circ}\) ki exact values nikal sakti hain? Haan! Aur is ke liye koi naya formula prove nahin karna, sirf \(\cos 2\alpha\) ki purani shaklon ko naye andaaz se dekhna hai.
Kitab kehti hai: oopar prove kiye gaye formulas ko half angle identities ki shakal mein bhi is tarah likha ja sakta hai:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Double angle formulas mein \(\alpha\), \(2\alpha\) ka aadha hai. Ab agar hum \(2\alpha\) ki jagah \(\alpha\) likhein, to \(\alpha\) ki jagah \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) aa jata hai. Yani \(\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\) ban jata hai \(\cos\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2} - 1\). Rishta wahi hai: ek angle aur us ka aadha. Ab sirf in equations ko \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\) aur \(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ke liye hal karna hai, bilkul jaise algebra mein \(x\) ke liye hal karte hain.

(i) \(\cos 2\alpha\) ki doosri shakal \(2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\) se shuru karte hain:
\[\cos\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2} - 1\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}}\]
Kya hua? Pehle dono taraf 1 jama kiya, phir 2 se divide kiya, aur aakhir mein square root liya. Square root lete hi \(\pm\) aa gaya, kyun ke kisi number ke do square roots hote hain.

blocks.text_alt: cos of alpha over 2 equals plus or minus the square root of (1 plus cos alpha) over 2

blocks.text:
(ii) Ab teesri shakal \(1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\) se:
\[\cos\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow \sin^{2}\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}\]
\[\Rightarrow \sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}\]
Yahan \(2\sin^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ko left aur \(\cos\alpha\) ko right le gaye, phir 2 se divide kar ke square root liya.

blocks.text_alt: sin of alpha over 2 equals plus or minus the square root of (1 minus cos alpha) over 2

blocks.text:
(iii) Tan to sin aur cos ka hissa (ratio) hai, is liye (ii) ko (i) se divide kar dein:
\[\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}} = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}}{\sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}}}\]
\[\Rightarrow \tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha}}\]
Dono roots ke neeche wala 2 aapas mein cancel ho gaya, aur ek hi root mein sab kuch aa gaya.

blocks.text_alt: tan of alpha over 2 equals plus or minus the square root of (1 minus cos alpha) over (1 plus cos alpha)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se ahem baat, sign ka faisla: formula khud nahin batata ke \(+\) lena hai ya \(-\). Yeh is baat par munhasir hai ke \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) kis quadrant mein hai. Ghor kariye, \(\alpha\) ka quadrant nahin, \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ka!
Misal: \(\alpha = 240^{\circ}\) lijiye. \(\cos 240^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Aadha angle \(\frac{\alpha}{2} = 120^{\circ}\), jo doosre quadrant mein hai, jahan cos negative hota hai. Is liye:
\[\cos 120^{\circ} = -\sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \frac{1}{2}}{2}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\]
Agar ghalti se \(+\) le lete to \(+\frac{1}{2}\) aata, jo ghalat hai. Is liye hamesha pehle likhiye: '\(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) kis quadrant mein hai?', phir sign chuniye.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Half angle identities ka sab se mashhoor istemal: \(\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) se \(15^{\circ}\) ki exact values:
\[\cos 15^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{3}}}{2}\]
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2 - \sqrt{3}}}{2}\]
\[\tan 15^{\circ} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{3}}{2 + \sqrt{3}}} = 2 - \sqrt{3}\]
Teeno jagah \(+\) liya kyun ke \(15^{\circ}\) pehle quadrant mein hai. Aakhri step mein upar neeche \(2 - \sqrt{3}\) se multiply kiya: neeche \(4 - 3 = 1\) bacha, aur root ke andar \((2 - \sqrt{3})^{2}\). Yeh jawab \(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}\) wale tareeqe se aane wali values \(\cos 15^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\), \(\sin 15^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}\) ke bilkul barabar hain; shakal alag, value ek.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab mein nahin, lekin bohat kaam ki baat: \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ki do aisi shaklein bhi hain jin mein root aur \(\pm\) nahin aata. \(\frac{\sin(\alpha/2)}{\cos(\alpha/2)}\) ke upar neeche \(2\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\) se multiply karein (ya \(2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\) se), aur double angle formulas lagayein:
\[\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha} = \dfrac{1 - \cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\]
In mein sign khud ba khud sahi aata hai, is liye quadrant ki uljhan nahin rehti.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: agar \(\cos\alpha = \frac{7}{25}\) aur \(0^{\circ} < \alpha < 90^{\circ}\), to \(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\) nikaaliye.
Pehle quadrant: \(0^{\circ} < \frac{\alpha}{2} < 45^{\circ}\), yani pehla quadrant, sab positive.
\(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - \frac{7}{25}}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{18/25}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{25}} = \frac{3}{5}\).
\(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \frac{7}{25}}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}} = \frac{4}{5}\).
\(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{18/25}{32/25}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3}{4}\).
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{3/5}{4/5} = \frac{3}{4}\), aur double angle se \(\cos\alpha = \cos^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2} - \sin^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{16 - 9}{25} = \frac{7}{25}\). Wapas wahi mil gaya!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\alpha = 180^{\circ}\) ho to \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ka formula kya kehta hai? \(\cos 180^{\circ} = -1\), to neeche \(1 + (-1) = 0\) aata hai. Matlab \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) defined nahin, jo hum pehle se jaante hain. Formula aur haqeeqat dono ek hi baat keh rahe hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Half angle identities, \(\cos 2\alpha\) ki shaklon \(2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\) aur \(1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\) ko \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ke liye likhne se banti hain.
2. \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}}\), \(\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{2}}\), \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2} = \pm\sqrt{\frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha}}\).
3. Andar plus ho to cos, andar minus ho to sin (double angle wala hi rule).
4. Sign hamesha \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\) ke quadrant se chuniye.
5. \(\tan\frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{\sin\alpha}{1 + \cos\alpha}\) wali shakal mein sign ki fikr nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Sign \(\alpha\) ke quadrant se chun lena. Misal: \(\alpha = 240^{\circ}\) teesre quadrant mein hai, lekin \(\frac{\alpha}{2} = 120^{\circ}\) doosre mein; sign 120 ke hisaab se lagega.
2. \(\frac{1 \pm \cos\alpha}{2}\) mein neeche wala 2 bhool jana. Tan wale formula mein yeh 2 cancel ho jata hai, lekin sin aur cos mein mojood hai.
3. Sin aur cos ke formulas mein \(1 + \cos\alpha\) aur \(1 - \cos\alpha\) aapas mein badal dena. Bachne ka tareeqa: \(\alpha = 0\) rakhiye; \(\cos 0 = 1\) aana chahiye, aur \(\sqrt{\frac{1+1}{2}} = 1\) sirf plus wale se aata hai.
4. \(\pm\) bilkul hi chhor dena. Jawab mein ya to sahi sign likhiye ya quadrant ki wazahat.
